text:
Locations January 21, 2018 Downsides of Tech products & Services Become a point of discussion for Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s CEO Tim Cook 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s CEO Tim Cook is most prominent in a long line of executives, and others in the tech industry, who openly talked about the downsides of technology products and services, and also have raised concerns. 
On Friday, Cook spoke about technology overuse, and saying that he wouldn’t allow his nephew, to use social networks, as technology adversely effects. 
Facebook’s former executive recently said that social media was “destroying how society works,” and iPhone’s inventor said that Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) and other tech firms should need to do more to address these concerns. 
The potential risks of modern technology, is not ignorable, as Tim Cook steps to limit his nephew’s use of technology, resemble those of other tech executives. 
Microsoft Corporation mogul “Bill Gates” said that he stopped his daughter’s screen time and also refused to let his children get the smartphones till age of 14. 
Cook’s predecessor as CEO of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) said right after the release of the iPad in 2010, that he had stopped his kids from using it. 
“We limit how much technology our kids use at home,” he said. 
While speaking on Friday, at a school in England, Cook said he didn’t want his nephew to use social media, according to The Guardian. He also argued that the use of tech in schools should be limited. 
“I don’t have a kid, but I have a nephew that I put some boundaries on,” Cook said, according to The Guardian. “There are some things that I won’t allow; I don’t want them on a social network.” 
He said he didn’t believe in overuse of technology, adding: “I’m not a person that says we’ve achieved success if you’re using it all the time I don’t subscribe to that at all.” 
“There are still concepts that you want to talk about and understand,” he said, according to the Guardian report. “In a course on literature, do I think you should use technology a lot? Probably not.” 
Now the tech industry, is also getting worried about what it has built for the people, as in recent months, there are numerous executives in the tech industry, have expressed the concerns about the side effect of technology on society and human minds. 
Sean Parker, the first president of Facebook, has charged that social networks are exploiting human “vulnerability,” saying: “God only knows what it’s doing to our children’s brains.” 
Chamath Palihapitiya, another former Facebook executive, said late last year that social media was “destroying how society works,” adding that he felt “tremendous guilt” for what he helped make. 
“In the back, deep, deep recesses of our mind, we kind of knew something bad could happen,” Palihapitiya said, though he later walked back parts of his remarks after they attracted significant international media attention. About Kevin Frahm
